The supplied juncture *and* is an obligatory English helper on the connective it introduces (rules 7, 29, 88), headed on *therefore* as the word glossing διό (rules 17, 91). Rule 88's verb pattern does not reach this: its closing line says an expressed Greek conjunction is untouched and aligned in the ordinary way, and the corpus has no unit giving a leading *and* to a finite verb an expressed conjunction precedes. The rule 29 family puts the juncture on whatever heads the member it introduces — JHN.19.20 *and in Greek* on an adverb, the *and ever* line on a noun — and 2CO's own connective frames (2CO.6.8, 2CO.6.9, 2CO.6.10, 2CO.11.9) are unhedged. `added` is foreclosed by rule 86, the conjunction being expressed, and the ASV does not italicize either *and*.

The expressed καί takes the English word standing in its slot, here the juncture *by* of the distributive *day by day*, and the two nouns stay split under rules 2 and 26. Rule 88's closing line governs: an expressed Greek conjunction is aligned in the ordinary way, and rules 29 and 30 do not reach it, their premise being a juncture with no Greek counterpart — which is why the neighbouring 2CO.4.17 εἰς ὑπερβολήν puts its supplied *and* on the member it introduces. A καί between two nouns runs 265 aligned to 1 unrepresented in the corpus, and that one is a rule 37 case; the English word need not be *and*, ἵνα taking *to* in 35 unhedged units. 2PE.2.8 ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας -> *from day to day* is the mirror, the expressed ἐξ taking *from* and only the supplied *to* riding with the noun. Medium under rule 93, the phrase being unattested: giving *by day* whole to the second noun remains defensible, but it is the weaker reading.

alignments.note: Rule 23: the ASV supplies no nominal for the article to take — *our* is ἡμῶν's, *light* is ἐλαφρόν's, *affliction* is θλίψεως' — so nothing is left for it. PHP.4.5 τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν -> *your forbearance* is the unhedged structural twin: substantival article over an adjective, free genitive pronoun, no supplied nominal, unrepresented. Rule 49's τὸ τρίτον -> *the third part* does not reach it, because there the ASV supplied *part* and wrote *of them* rather than a possessive. Medium is for the rule 31 reading, which would give the article the supplied *which* — the same seam the παραυτίκα unit concedes.

The adverb is expanded into a supplied finite relative clause *which is for the moment*; with no verb and no preposition in the Greek, the adverb carries the relativizer, copula and determiner as rule 7 helpers, headed on *moment* as its own gloss (rules 53, 91). Giving *which* to the article under rule 31 remains defensible, and the corpus does put a bare *which is* on an attributive article in 4 of its 5 such units (REV.10.8, REV.11.2, REV.14.17, REV.9.13); that is the one seam this medium and s001's are both paying for.

Rule 2 splits the phrase and rule 34 empties the preposition: no English word answers to καθ᾽ separately, and GAL.1.13 splits this very phrase καθ᾽ ὑπερβολήν. The pair was one aligned unit, but every aligned PREP+X unit in the corpus renders to exactly one English word, so an aligned compound spanning *and more exceedingly* had no precedent anywhere; splitting both phrases keeps them symmetric. Medium: reading all four tokens as one noncompositional unit on *more and more exceedingly* remains defensible (JHN.19.18 is that shape), though rule 6 reserves that status for the genuinely indivisible and the ASV's *more … and more* tracks the Greek doubling. The corpus is divided on a κατά phrase English realizes nowhere: 2CO.11.28 καθ᾽ ἡμέραν -> *daily* is noncompositional, also medium and also conceding.

ὑπερβολήν takes the first *more* of the distributive *more and more exceedingly*. Rule 91 cannot decide the head between *more* and *exceedingly*, the corpus spending neither on this lexeme, which is the second reason for medium.

Substantival article before a participle, taking the nominal expression under rules 22 and 32 and headed on the nominal word. The supplied *at* stays with the article on the strength of PHP.2.4, which is this exact shape — σκοπέω with coordinate substantival τὰ objects and the preposition repeated on each member, resolved on the articles at high — and because the verb has no workable target for it: the ASV writes *at* twice, once per object across ἀλλά, and rule 15 forbids absorbing that span into σκοπούντων, which no corpus verb unit does. Medium is real: the contrary line puts the particle on the verb (JHN.4.35 *look on*, REV.18.9 and REV.18.18 *look upon*, the last deciding this very question against the article), and rule 21's licence is for a case preposition, which an accusative direct object does not need. Note this is not the same construction as 4.9 *smitten down* or 4.10 *bearing about*, where the particle governs nothing and renders the verb's own prefix.
